reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Using stage letters without the sellar grade.
name: Hardy Classification of Pituitary Adenomas (modified by Wilson)

version.label: Hardy sellar grades 0–IV with Wilson's extrasellar stages A–E
version.detail: Sellar floor changes (Hardy) and suprasellar/parasellar extension (Wilson's modification). Wording of the extrasellar stages varies between reproductions.

purpose: Describes sellar destruction and extrasellar extension of pituitary adenomas.
intendedPopulation: Patients with pituitary adenoma on MRI or CT.

options.label: Grade 0: Intrapituitary microadenoma; normal sellar floor
Grade I: Normal-sized sella with focal asymmetry or bulging of the floor
Grade II: Enlarged sella with an intact floor
Grade III: Localised erosion or destruction of the sellar floor
Grade IV: Diffuse destruction of the sellar floor
A: Bulges into the suprasellar (chiasmatic) cistern
B: Reaches or obliterates the recesses of the floor of the third ventricle
C: Large extension displacing the third ventricle up to the foramen of Monro
D: Intracranial intradural extension into anterior, middle or posterior fossa
E: Extradural extension into or beneath the cavernous sinus

resultStates.label: Grade {g_code}{x_code == '0' ? '' : ', stage ' + x_code}
resultStates.summary: Sellar grades II–IV correspond to macroadenomas.

clinicalContext.text: Combines sellar floor destruction with the direction of extrasellar extension.

clinicalInsights.text: Stages D–E indicate intracranial or cavernous sinus extension; see Knosp for cavernous sinus invasion.

limitations.text: Developed in the radiograph/CT era; MRI-based Knosp grading is preferred for cavernous sinus invasion.

limitations: Extrasellar stage wording differs between sources.

guideSections.what: Sellar grades 0–IV with extrasellar stages A–E.
guideSections.howToPerform: Grade the sellar floor; then assign the extrasellar extension.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with Knosp grade, hormones and visual fields.

sources.citation: Hardy J. Transsphenoidal microsurgery of the normal and pathological pituitary. Clin Neurosurg. 1969;16:185-217.
Wilson CB. Neurosurgical management of large and invasive pituitary tumors. In: Tindall GT, Collins WF, eds. Clinical Management of Pituitary Disorders. New York: Raven Press; 1979:335-342.
